proposed_comments.title: Reject out-of-range recording scale values

confidence.rationale: The DSC setter serializes the supplied value directly, the Settings UI clamps the effective display range to 10–100, and native recording uses the persisted value to scale frame dimensions.

proposed_comments.title: Validate native recording-format writes

confidence.rationale: The native conversion explicitly maps every non-GIF string to MP4, while the added tests replace the native save delegate and only call the real interop for a read.

proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The faulty native RecordFormat conversion is in pre-existing ZoomItSettingsInterop code that this PR does not change; the new test file also cannot exercise the native save path without a registry/test seam.
proposed_comments.body:
### Validate native recording-format writes

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/ZoomIt/ZoomItSettingsInterop/ZoomItSettings.cpp` (`ZoomItSettings::SaveSettingsJson`) and `src/dsc/v3/PowerToys.DSC.UnitTests/SettingsResourceTests/SettingsResourceZoomItModuleTest.cs` (`TestInitialize`, `Interop_LoadSettingsJson_DeserializesIntoSettingsModel`).

**Problem:** The native `RecordFormat` conversion maps `GIF` to 0 and every other string to 1 (`MP4`), then persists the setting. The added unit tests replace `SaveSettingsJson` with an in-memory delegate; their real-interoperability test only reads settings, so this native write behavior is not covered.

**Why it matters:** A misspelled or unsupported format can report a successful DSC set while silently switching ZoomIt to MP4, and the current tests cannot detect the native conversion or a regression in rejecting malformed values.

**Suggested change:**
1. Validate a supplied `RecordFormat` before mutating any native settings. Accept only `GIF` and `MP4`, and return an invalid-argument error for any other non-null value instead of coercing it to MP4.
2. Add an isolated native-save test seam or registry fixture so the real interop validation can be exercised without writing to the developer's ZoomIt settings. Verify both supported formats and verify an unknown format is rejected before registry state changes.

**Verification:** Build `ZoomItSettingsInterop` and `PowerToys.DSC` in Debug x64, then run the focused ZoomIt DSC unit tests. Confirm valid formats save, invalid input fails, and the test leaves the user's registry settings unchanged.

proposed_comments.title: Fix the StyleCop blank-line violation

confidence.rationale: The exact upstream DSC build fails with SA1515 at this newly added comment; inserting the required blank line is a deterministic build fix.

proposed_comments.body:
### Fix the StyleCop blank-line violation

**Severity:** `low`

The exact upstream DSC build reports `SA1515` on this comment because it follows the `Workspaces` registration without a separating blank line. Add the required blank line before the ZoomIt comment and rerun the DSC build.

```suggestion

            // ZoomIt stores its settings in the registry rather than in settings.json
```

proposed_comments.title: Isolate the refresh-event test from the production event

confidence.rationale: The test and the running ZoomIt instance open the same auto-reset event, and the test explicitly resets and waits on that shared event.

proposed_comments.body:
### Isolate the refresh-event test from the production event

**Severity:** `medium`

This test creates, resets, and waits on `RefreshSettingsEventName`, the same auto-reset event ZoomIt creates and waits on. If ZoomIt is running, it and the test can consume the single signal, and `Reset()` can clear a pending production notification. Inject the refresh signal or event into `ZoomItSettingsFunctionData` and assert against a test-owned event or callback instead of touching the production name.
